articleTitle: Measurement and analysis of partial discharge of high and medium voltage power equipment
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: The partial discharge measurement is gradually becoming an important preventing maintenance for power apparatuses with voltage level of higher than medium voltage. In practical, however, field measurement of partial discharge is easily suffered by interferences. The measurement compatible to the apparatuses and environmental features should be considered and different discharge models should be analyzed. This paper is aimed to measure partial discharge of medium voltage power equipment under use. Firstly, the measurement method by using high frequency current transformer (HFCT) is introduced, and then, the various partial discharges including internal discharge, along-surface discharge and tip discharge are modeled and energized to measurement. Furthermore, the discharge waveform features and phase distribution characteristics are analyzed for identifying the type of partial discharge. The measurement and analysis results for actual case are compared with the standard discharge pattern data of laboratory, which show that the proposed measurement and analysis have well representative. This can provide the basis for the establishment of the partial discharge database of medium voltage power equipment, which is also required for development of partial discharge automatic identification system.

articleTitle: An efficient hand detection method based on convolutional neural network
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an efficient method for detecting human hands based on the architecture of YOLO [1]. By utilizing the spatial-transfer connection (STC) between high-level layers and low-level layers, the multi-scale features from different layers can be aggregated for detecting the hands. Experimental results on the Hand Dataset [2] show that the proposed architecture can improve efficiency and achieves better results than YOLO when detecting small objects such as human hands.

articleTitle: An active gate driver for improving switching performance of SiC MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: An active gate driver (AGD) is presented in this work for Silicon Carbide (SiC) devices to fully utilize their potential of high-speed characteristic in higher power density and higher efficiency applications. It can actively adjust the drive voltage during the switching transient of SiC MOSFET and with simple circuit implementation. Compared to the conventional gate driver (CGD) with fixed drive voltage, the proposed method has the capability of increasing the switching speed while minimizing the switching stress. The operation principle of the proposed AGD and control concept are introduced in detail. Finally, based on 1200V/19A SiC MOSFETs from CREE, experimental verification is carried out in double pulse test to illustrate the proposed AGD and the obtained results indeed verify its superiority than the CGD.

articleTitle: Application of a minimized wearable device combined with SpO2 and ECG sensors to detect stenosis or occlusion of arteriovenous fistula/graft, progression of arteriosclerosis and arrhythmia
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Stroke is a common disease in modern society, which is the occluded and/or hemorrhaging of the blood vessels in the brain, producing blood clots leading to brain dysfunctions. When faced with the risk of stroke, most people tend to measure their blood pressure first; however, aside from hypertension, vessel atherosclerosis and loss of elasticity are also the causes for blood vessel stenosis and/or rupturing. Additionally, in dialysis patients, prolonged needle puncture will also decrease vessel elasticity, which leads to increased stenosis of hemodialysis access and ineffective hemodialysis. In this study, we proposed a method to integrate and analyze signals measured from SpO2 and ECG sensors to detect blood vessel elasticity and stenosis. Our proposed system has advantages in size and cost, is portable and allows patients to record real-time and long-term blood vessel health status. Our method is a non-invasive measurement of the physiological signals, which can rapidly analyze the stenosis of hemodialysis access, and to take long-term records. The data collected can be analyzed by physicians for precision medicine and preventative health.

articleTitle: Singing voice detection based on convolutional neural networks
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper investigates various structures of convolutional neural networks (CNN) for singing voice detection. The input features are MFCC (mel-frequency cepstrum coefficients), DFT (discrete Fourier transform) coefficients, and raw PCM samples. The simulation results show that DFT coefficients yields higher detection accuracy, up to 92%.

articleTitle: Device design of vertical nanowire III-V heterojunction TFETs for performance enhancement
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the heterojunction GaAs<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.4</sub>Sb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.6</sub>/In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.65</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.35</sub>As TFET with vertical nanowire structure and non-uniform diameter design (V-NW TFET with non-uniform diameter). A thin channel layer (Ti) is inserted between the gate and source regions for improving the on currents, and the non-uniform diameter thickness is used for suppressing the leakage current (I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">min</sub>). The bandgap widening induced by quantum confinement is considered in this work. The leakage current can be suppressed by using thinner diameter thickness of the drain/channel junction (T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DC</sub>), and the gate-to-drain underlap design is used to further reduce the ambipolar leakage. The impacts of Ti, T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DC</sub>, source and drain doping concentrations, and gate-to-source overlap length (L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ovs</sub>) on the V-NW TFET have been investigated. Compared with the ultra-thin body (UTB) TFET, the proposed V-NW TFET with non-uniform diameter (thin T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DC</sub>) exhibits 2 times larger I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</sub> (236 μA/μm) due to the increased line tunneling area, and 59.8 times lower leakage current (5.5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-10</sup> μA/μm).

articleTitle: Solution of the optimal reactive power dispatch for power systems by using novel charged system search algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Proper reactive power dispatch can not only reduce the active power loss, but also can improve the voltage stability, and make the system operate in the security operation range. In this paper, we use intelligent control method is used to implement optimal reactive power dispatch for IEEE30-bus and IEEE57-bus systems. And we use three types of optimization algorithms to compare: Charged System Search (CSS), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Hybrid Charged System Search and Particle Swarm Optimization (HCSSPSO). Analysis of reactive power dispatch benefits. In this paper, the optimal objective function is to minimize the loss rate in the transmission line, and satisfies all the constraints of the system, be sure to consider the optimal objective function range of within a reasonable. From the simulation results, HCSSPSO can get the global optimal solution faster than CSS and PSO. Therefore, the times of solve can be reduced and the global optimal solution can be obtained more easily. Through the analysis of both the IEEE 30-bus and IEEE 57-bus systems, it is demonstrated that the optimization method used is feasible for reactive power dispatch, reducing the active power loss in the transmission line and keeping the load bus voltage range of within a reasonable. Expect to help dispatchers make more economical and secure dispatch.

Author Keywords: Hybrid Charged System Search and Particle Swarm Optimization

articleTitle: A single GaN HEMT oscillator with four-path inductors
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This letter proposes a single GaN HEMT oscillator implemented with the WIN 0.25 μm GaN HEMT technology. The oscillator consists of a HEMT amplifier with an LC feedback network. The inductor uses four-path inductor with high Q-factor. With the supply voltage of V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DD</sub> = 2 V, the GaN VCO current and power consumption of the oscillator are 10.8 mA and 21.6mW, respectively. The oscillator can generate single-ended signal at 8.82 GHz and it also supplies output power 1.24 dBm. At 1MHz frequency offset from the carrier the phase noise is -124.95 dBc/Hz. The die area of the GaN HEMT oscillator is 2×1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Evaluation of routability-driven macro placement with machine-learning technique
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Macro placement is an important step in floor-plan. Macros' location directly affects the next steps, cells placement and wires routing. However, it is a time-consuming work to evaluate macro placement's result. To address this problem, we propose an effective evaluation method with machine learning technique. Our methodology predicts HPWL and routing congestion after macro placement, rather than after cells placement and global routing. Therefore, it takes much short time that we can get HPWL and routing congestion. Experiment results show that our evaluation is accurate and effective.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of micro hotplate based metal oxide nanowire gas sensor
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Increase in the emission of hazardous and toxic gases from vehicles, industries, etc. has led to the increase in environmental pollution. An exposure to these gases even in trace level will cause serious health issue and is threatening for day to day life. Hence, detection and taking corrective measures for reducing the gases is of utmost significance. Metal oxide semiconductor based sensors are widely used for gas sensing due to low cost and low power consumptions. In this paper, we have simulated a zinc oxide nanowire based gas sensor for detecting carbon monoxide gas as it is the most common fatal air poisoning gas in many countries. The response of the zinc oxide nanowires to carbon monoxide gas was monitored and evaluated the surface resistance with respect to the concentration and operating temperature.

articleTitle: Ternary sparse XNOR-Net for FPGA implementation
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In general, the more product sum circuits are used, the higher the recognition accuracy is when deep learning is applied to the circuits. Therefore, the circuit scale and power consumption inevitably need to be increased. That is why deep learning is difficult to apply in the IoT. Binary XNOR-Net is a method that is conventionally considered to be the smallest circuit scale. Ternary Sparse XNOR-Net was designed for this research. It improves the recognition accuracy by ternarizing the weight data as (−1, 0, 1). Furthermore, when implementing it in the FPGA, the wiring itself is not mounted only in the part with weight 0. Through this sparse connection, the circuit size was reduced by 73% compared with that of the conventional method, while the recognition precision also improved about 1 to 3% in each neuron number.

articleTitle: A segmented resistor-string DAC based stimulus generator for ADC linearity testing
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper presents a segmented resistor-string digital-to-analog converter (DAC) based stimulus generator for analog-to-digital converter (ADC) linearity testing. By using the folded main resistor string, the capacitive loading is reduced to enhance the operating speed of the DAC. The complexity, the number of unit resistors, and the area cost of the DAC are reduced by using the parallel-connected sub-resistor strings. The theoretical analyses of the area cost, settling behavior, and the integral/differential non-linearities (INL/DNL) are presented to evaluate the trade-offs among the performance of the proposed DAC, the design parameter, and the mismatch of the resistor. Due to the features of simple structure and low capacitance loading, the proposed DAC is combined with a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) device and other circuitry to practically generate a ramp stimulus for ADC linearity testing. The testing result by using the proposed segmented DAC based stimulus generator shows a certain agreement to that by using the expensive instrument.

articleTitle: FPGA realization of activation function for neural network
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper presents the FPGA implementation of neuron block units based on a sigmoid activation function for artificial neural networks (ANNs) applications. The proposed system was simulated using Modelsim XE II and synthesized using Synopsys design compiler based on TSMC 90 nm technology file. The functionality of backward propagation was successfully verified as compared with the python simulation results.

articleTitle: Hardware design on FPGA for Ethernet/SONET bridge in smart sensor system
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper presents a packet bridge between Ethernet and Synchronous Optical Network (SONET) with format transformation in smart sensor system. The transformed packet can be fed to the optical fiber, which proceeds with various features such as high speed, long distance, and low interference. With SONET, the packet bridge performs with high speed, long distance, low interference, and good-property in sensor system, whereas the bridge works without those features in electrical transmission. The packet bridge is designed and implemented with Verilog Hardware Description Language (HDL) and verified with FPGA development board with RS485 serial port. Measured results show that the operation frequency, throughput, data transfer rate of RS485, and data transfer rate of Ethernet are 125 MHz, 633,661,952 bps, 115,200 bps, and 1 Gbps, respectively, at the data volume of 8 bits, a RAM of 2 k bytes, and a FIFO of 1 k bytes.

articleTitle: A digitally variable on-time controlled PFC flyback converter with primary-side regulation
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In this paper, a digital variable on-time control (VOT) and primary side regulation (PSR) applied to a power factor correction (PFC) flyback converter is realized. This PFC flyback converter is operated in the critical conduction mode (CRM). Compared with constant on-time control (COT), VOT control can decrease total harmonic distortion (THD) of input current and make high power factor (PF). The method which is used to obtain output voltage is PSR. This method can sense output voltage by auxiliary wind without opto-coupler. This PFC flyback converter worked in universal input voltage 90~264Vac and the output power is 36W with output DC voltage 36V. The proposed control method is implemented by field-programmable gate array (FPGA). Experimental result are shown that PF is higher than 0.95 and THD is less than 10%.

articleTitle: Impact of the gate structure on ESD characteristic of tunnel field-effect transistors
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Tunnel field-effect transistor (TFET) is a promising candidate in replacing a MOSFET, particularly for the next generation low-power integrated circuits (ICs). The gate grounded TFET (ggTFET) is considered as a basic electrostatic discharge (ESD) protection device in the TFET ICs. In this work, the impact of the gate structure on the ESD characteristic of the TFETs has been investigated using TCAD simulation. It is found that the technology parameters such as gate length, gate oxide thickness, and gate structure geometry affect both the triggering voltage and the failure current of the TFET.

articleTitle: Proximity capacitive gesture recognition for a adaptive fuzzy neural network
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper presented an adaptive fuzzy neural network (AFNN) user gesture base on proximity capacitive sensor. The human interactive gesture signal analyses have been a research topic smart home fields that algorithms build in local device to recognize real time. The fuzzy and neural network have been used in many fields that including identification, control and classification. Neural network features is used neurons weight train and learn target results, and fuzzy features used fuzzy membership function to fuzzification input signal. Therefore, the AFNN methods to identify user gesture has satisfactory response.

articleTitle: A vision-based nighttime surrounding vehicle detection system
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This study proposes a vision-based nightime surrounding nighttime vehicle detection system implemented by automatic multilevel thresholding method, denoise, connected component labeling, head light matching method, and head light tracking and classification. It is able to detect head light position, and get the vehicle position. Testing by four videos that we have record while we were driving, for side view, accuracy are all higher than 90%, and the time cost are all higher than 140 frames per second; for rear view, accuracy are all higher than 90%, and the time cost are all higher than 85 frames per second. By this system, we can make sure that there is any vehicle surrounding or not. If there is, it will decide which kind of vehicle it is, and notice the driver with different level, to supply more information and longer reaction time for driver, in order to decrease accident rate, increase driving safety.

articleTitle: Stochastic weights binary neural networks on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: To achieve an advanced Internet of Things (IoT), it is necessary to combine artificial intelligence (AI) with IoT. Compact circuits that can operate AI functions will be useful for this purpose. Therefore, we propose stochastic weights binary neural networks (SWBNN). SWBNNs are more accurate than binary neural networks (BNN) with small circuits. BNNs can be realized with small circuits since binary calculation needs simpler circuits than real number calculation. However, BNNs have lower accuracy than networks with real numbers. Thus, the proposed SWBNNs are BNNs that behave stochastically, which makes them more accurate than BNNs. Moreover, SWBNNs can still be achieved with small circuits since they execute binary calculation. As a result, the accuracy for the test data of SWBNNs is closer to the accuracy for learning data than the accuracy for the test data of BNNs is. Especially when using the CIFAR10 database, the difference in the identification accuracy rate between learning data and test data decreased from 6% for BNNs to 2% for SWBNNs. From results of a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) implementation, circuits of SWBNNs are sufficiently small although they are 10% bigger than those of BNNs. Therefore, SWBNNs are more accurate than BNNs, and the circuit costs ofintroducing stochastic weights are low.

articleTitle: An improved reference voltage circuit design
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In this paper, an improved reference voltage circuit has been proposed. Unlike the traditional works, in the proposed circuit, the positive temperature coefficient voltage is obtained from the BJT but the negative temperature coefficient voltage is from the weak-inversion biased MOSFETs. Proper combination of the positive and negative temperature-coefficient voltages, a zero temperature-coefficient reference voltage can be given. The proposed reference voltage has been layout by using the 2P4M 0.35μm process parameters. According to the post-layout simulation results, when the supply voltage is 1.7 V, the corresponding power consumption is 24.18 μW, the output reference voltage can be around 488 mV, and as the temperature varies from -20 °C to 120 °C, the temperature coefficient of the proposed reference voltage is only 8.336 ppm/°C. As compared to the traditional works, the proposed circuit benefits from simpler circuit architecture, less chip area, and smaller temperature coefficient. The proposed reference voltage circuit can be applied to various analog integrated circuits applications.

articleTitle: The car door safety system with wireless alert transmission
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper presents a car door safety system which has two major features: 1) sense objects when car door is opened with audio and visible light warning, 2) transmit alert by low power wireless communication which a technology based on IEEE 802.11ah named Sigfox has been chosen when the crash detected. The car door safety system which this paper presented is based on popular microcontrollers and sensors, it is easy to build, integrate and low cost.

articleTitle: The influence of IoT data encapsulation on transmission and energy : A case study on wearable smart shoes
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: More and more devices, e.g., wearable devices, are interconnected to form the Internet of Things (IoT). However, these devices are limited to their network bandwidth and battery power. This paper implements one wearable smart shoes and then discuss and evaluate how to encapsulate data to fit the limited IoT environment. Based on our experimental results, only the data features are suitable to be passed through the wireless network if the data is formatted to any standardized IoT format.

articleTitle: The voice controlled Internet of Things system
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper presents an Internet of Things (IoT) system which is controlled by human voice and natural language, including appliance and indoor environment sensor. The appliances will be bundled with a socket controlled by relay and a MediaTek LinkIt 7697, which is marketed Arduino compatible development board. The environment sensor was DHT11, a marketed indoor environment sensor, which also bundled with a MediaTek LinkIt 7697. The protocol to communicate with both MediaTek LinkIt 7697 is Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT). The gateway for this IoT application is a QBoat Sunny, it is home IoT gateway of Taiwan QNAP Corp. which has built-in Linux and numerous functions. Based on these functions, the IoT system can access voice recognition and natural language parsing functions of Google to accomplish the jobs.

articleTitle: Droplet epitaxy and its possibilities in nano-electronics
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In this work, we are dealing with a novel technology, called droplet epitaxy, which is useful technique when quantum dots are to be produced, of different shape and size in various densities. There are self-assembling methods to achieve quantum dot ensembles and their spatial ordering and positioning. Their evolution kinetic is very important to handheld the self-assembling. After the discussion of the growth mechanism, we are dealing some of self-assembled quantum dot arrangement in the view point of realization of nano-electronics.

articleTitle: The voice controlled Internet of Things system
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)

articleTitle: A 10-bit 200-MS/s switched-current pipelined ADC for analog front end of XDSL
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper presents a 10-bit 200-Msample/s switched-current (SI) pipelined analog-to-digital converter (ADC) for analog front-end (AFE) of XDSL. In the proposed switched-current sample-and-hold circuit (SH), the current mirror is designed with active feedback and dummy switch to improve the accuracy of pipelined ADC by decreasing the transmission error and channel charge injection. The post-simulation results show that the signal-to-noise and distortion ratio (SNDR) is 61.07 dB whose effective number of bit (ENOB) is about 9.85 bits at the input frequency of 5 MHz, the sampling rate of 200 MHz, the power consumption of 56 mW, and the supply voltage of 1.8 V. Note that the figure of merit (FoM) is roughly 0.3 pJ/conversion at the operational current ranging from -20 μA to +20μA. The proposed ADC is fabricated in TSMC 1P6M 0.18μm CMOS process and its chip area is 1.2×1.2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (with I/O pad).

articleTitle: P16INK4a detection using an ultra-sensitive silicon nanowire field effect transistor
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In general, if cancer can be earlier detected and treated, the chance of recovery is relatively much higher. Among all advanced molecular diagnostic techniques, silicon nanowire field effect transistor sensors have proven to have extremely high sensitivity and specificity. Through side-wall spacer etch technique which possesses simpler and cheaper process steps to manufacture polycrystalline silicon nanowire field effect transistor sensor. And p16<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">INK4a</sup> protein which is related to cervical cancer, is taken as the target of detection. When human is infected with high-risk HPV, p16<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">INK4a</sup> protein will be overexpressed. Therefore, we can know the extent of HPV infection by detecting p16<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">INK4a</sup> protein, and then assess whether there is the risk of cervical cancer.

articleTitle: Optical and photo-electrical properties of zinc tin oxide thin-film phototransistor
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: We investigated the optical and electrical properties of the zinc tin oxide (ZTO) thin-film phototransistors. The device has a threshold voltage of 0.48 V, field effect mobility of 1.47 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/Vs in the saturation region, on/off drain current ratio of 2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>, and subthreshold swing of 0.45 V/decade under dark environment. As an UV photodetector, the device has a responsivity of 0.329 A/W and a rejection ratio of 3.19×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> at a gate voltage of -15 V under illumination of wavelength 300 nm.

articleTitle: Program plagiarism detection with dynamic structure
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: The paper proposed an automated program alignment system, SPDS (Structure Plagiarism Detection System) which allows users to determine whether there is any possibility of plagiarism among them. The dynamic slicing was used to analyze the behavior of the function, combining the combinatorial decision coverage to generate valid inputs, and convert the results to the program dependence graph to calculate the similarity of the behavioral part. The similarity of the variable and comment are calculated by cosine similarity and winnowing algorithm. Finally, the weight of each similarity can be adjusted by the user or decided by the system depends on the different situation. The experimental result shows that our proposed system can have better similarity measure result than JPlag, MOSS, and SPD.

articleTitle: An energy-saving scheme of TWDM-PON system for NG-EPON networks
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Time and wavelength-division multiplexed passive optical network (TWDM-PON) is a primary solution for the next-generation passive optical network. Previous works in TWDM-PON mainly adopt dual energy-saving modes in ONUs for serving downstream traffic. Such approach may lead to significant energy waste. This paper proposes a cycle-based tri-mode energy-saving mechanism by jointly considering both packet arrival time and tuning time, to achieve enhanced energy saving and delay performance. Simulation results show that proposed scheme saves the energy on both ONU and OSU while providing satisfactory QoS performance.

articleTitle: Analysis of heterojunction GaAs1−xSbx/In1−yGayAs tunnel FETs considering line tunneling
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In this work, we analyze the heterojunction GaAsi-xSbx/Ini-yGayAs Tunnel FETs (TFETs) with various material compositions and effective tunneling barriers (E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">beff</sub>) considering line tunneling. An epitaxial channel layer is placed between source and gate dielectric (TFET with T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">epi</sub>) to introduce the line tunneling which increases the on current significantly compared with the conventional p-i-n TFET with point tunneling only. The current components of TFET with T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">epi</sub> consist of both vertical line tunneling and lateral point tunneling. The onset voltage of line tunneling is defined as the gate voltage at which the drain current is dominated by line tunneling. The onset voltage of line tunneling can be reduced as E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">beff</sub> decreases. Therefore, for TFET with T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">epi</sub> and smaller E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">beff</sub>, the on current improvements owing to the increased gate-to-source overlap length (Lovs) are more significant than that with larger E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">beff</sub>. As Lovs increases, the drain currents contributed by vertical line tunneling are enhanced due to the increased tunneling area, while the drain currents contributed by lateral point tunneling are suppressed due to the increased tunneling width. Heterojunction GaAs<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Sb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>/In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-y</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sub>As TFET with T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">epi</sub> should be designed with smaller E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">beff</sub> to gain advantage of line tunneling.

articleTitle: Measured near field communication antenna for Fintech innovation
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper propose qualified near field communication antenna by LDS (Laser Direct Structuring) type with a via-hole Balun on mobile or wearable system to support Fintech (Financial technology) application.

articleTitle: Three-level PWM for grid-connected PV inverter considering switching loss and common-mode voltage
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) power generation has attracted many attentions for a decade. Both two-level and three-level inverters are commonly used topologies to feed the power into the three-phase electric grid system. Further, the three-level neutral point clamped inverter is always applied to the transformerless photovoltaic grid-connected system because of its low leakage current and the low voltage stress comparing with the two-level inverters. In the transformerless grid-connected PV inverter system, both reliability and the efficiency are important factors. Because of no isolation, the common-mode voltage of the inverter must be low to prevent adverse effects from the leakage current. Further, the switching loss must be low to have high efficiency. In this paper, a low switching loss PWM strategy with low common-mode voltage applied to three-level grid-tied inverter is shown. Comparing with the conventional carrier-based phase disposition PWM, both common-mode voltage and the switching loss are improved.

articleTitle: Detection of low wall motion and comparison study with scar tissue using 4D left ventricle cardiac images
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: The myocardial contraction creates an effective cardiovascular pumping system. While regional dysfunction of myocardium leads to functional abnormality of cardiac wall motion that is one of the risk factors for ventricular remodeling. It helps in the early phase detecting abnormalities of wall motion while wall motion of cardiac cycle make difficult to observe without any physical reference point. In this research, we find to characterize regional systolic function abnormalities. In house developed 4D image processing software that extracts the wall motion of left ventricle from a 4D cardiac images. We created 10 frames of 3D heart model that contains long axis as reference for predicting left ventricle wall motion. We tested our model with Scar tissue to 4D cardiac model of left ventricle, low motion area as non-invasive method of early detection. The detection in wall motion could effectively reflect the dysfunction of myocardium. Thus, this study provides a new approach to assess the degree and site dysfunction area of myocardium.

articleTitle: On-road weather detection and analysis based on visual models
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to develop a system to automatically detect weather and daytime based on visual models, including the use of image pre-processing technology, visual machine technology, machine learning technology, SVM to distinguish between weather and daytime, to provide a set of technologies To improve driving safety.

articleTitle: Tunneling leakage current reduction in junctionless transistors using a lightly doped region near drain
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: A novel double gate junctionless transistor with a lightly doped region near drain (LD-JLT) is investigated through two-dimensional numerical simulations and compared with the conventional double gate junctionless transistor (C-JLT). Simulation results show that the OFF-state current of our proposed LD-JLT is more than eight orders smaller than that of the C-JNT due to the increased tunneling barrier width and reduced band-to-band-tunneling (BTBT) generation rate. Furthermore, the channel length dependency of the LD-JLT and the C-JLT shows that our proposed LD-JLT exhibits superior scaling capability.

articleTitle: Disposable PEDOT:PSS-modifìed graphene electrochemical biosensor
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene): polystyrene-sulfonic acid (PEDOT:PSS), a conducting polymer, has attracted much attention in biosensor development due to its high bio-receptor immobilization capacity, good conductivity, high stability and biocompatibility. Graphene is a highly promising material for electrochemical sensing because it possesses a much larger specific surface area and an excellent electrical conductivity. In this work, we demonstrated a PEDOT:PSS modified screen-printed graphene electrode as a practically useful material platform for highly sensitive electrochemical detection.

articleTitle: Real time distributed generation monitoring at substation based on feeder IED functions and load profiles
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper applied MATLAB/Simulink to construct a typical distribution power system and two distributed generation systems which were connected to feeder, by observing the value of intelligent electronic device (IED) about current variation of substation and feeder under different solar irradiances and temperatures, monitoring and maintenance personnel could confirm the situation about photovoltaic generation system remotely. In this way, IED could be used as protection apparatus and maximized operation performance.

articleTitle: Integrated antenna with balun design for Miracast
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper proposed combo antenna near field communication (NFC), Felica or Mifare and WiFi Bluetooth antenna by LDS type with a via-hole Balun on smartphone or tablet PC Miracast system to support wireless communication network information and detect WLAN WPAN signal application on Smart Phone Miracast. FDTD simulation results and measurement can meet Miracast, RFID payment performance and requirement for wireless communication networking solutions management. This provides has good design from antenna radiation performance point of view for wearable technologies. The simulations and method for measuring the circuit parameters by means of impedance analyzer measurements is proposed. A comparison of the obtained values is presented for wearable application.

articleTitle: Rotation memory neural network identify elders fall situation
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper presented a rotation memory neural network identify elders fall situation in wearable device. The older human signal analysis have been a research topic health care fields that algorithms build in wearable device real time detect fall situation. However, the wearable device system code size is limited. Therefore, we utilize rotation memory methods to adjust weight that simplify tradition self-organizing neural network. In the experimental results, the rotation memory neural network identify human fall signal. In addition, we used wearable device combined BLE (Bluetooth low energy) feedback output response real time.

articleTitle: Divide-by-2 injection-locked frequency divider using distributed spiral resonator: 2:1 distributed spiral resonator injection-locked frequency divider
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper investigates the locking range property of a divide-by-2 RLC cross-coupled injection-locked frequency divider (ILFD). The ILFD uses a RLC resonator and it is originally targeting for having two overlapped locking ranges at 0 dB m injection power. At the power consumption 4.57 mW and at the incident power of 0 dBm, the locking range of this NFET ILFD is 7.94 GHz, from the injection frequency 2.2 GHz to 10.14 GHz. At low injection power, the ILFD can have two or three non-overlapped locking ranges, indicating that the on-chip spiral inductor shows the effect of distributed capacitance and the ILFD uses a distributed spiral resonator.

articleTitle: DRAM refresh improvement with bank reordering
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Due to few cells in memory that have lower retention time, DRAM have to raise the refresh frequency to keep the data integrity, and produce unnecessary refresh for the other normal cells, which result in large refresh power consumption and the delay of memory access. In this paper, we propose a DRAM bank reordering technique to considering the randomness of weak row distribution. We resolve this problem by the mixed integer linear programming methodology to achieve the best bank order that have the lowest refresh overhead. Experimental results show that with the bank reordering technique, we can reduce more refresh power and get even performance improvement than without applying it.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of a 3.85–5.23 GHz linear-tuning CMOS LC-tank VCO
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Design and analysis of a highly linear-tuning CMOS LC-tank voltage-controlled oscillator was presented in this paper. A single tuning resonant tank with a distribution MOS varactor biasing pair and the 2bits binary-weighted band-switching capacitors is proposed to reduce the variation of tuning sensitivity and cover 31% tuning range from 3.85GHz to 5.23GHz. The simulated phase noise is -115.3dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset frequency from 5.23GHz carrier. The proposed VCO core consumes 4.5mA current at 1.8V supply voltage. The whole chip area is 1.0μm × 0.95μm by using TSMC 0.18μm CMOS process.

articleTitle: Investigation of the DNA droplet CMOS/MEMS chip microfluidic channels geometry
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This research is focused on investigation of the DNA droplet chip channel geometry and size microfluidic channels. The life span of DNA bead sprayers is a considerable improvement. Bead generation architecture is designed to spray two-channel microfluid conical cavity structure. It operates in 10KHz mode. This microchannel is a multi-dimensional side view observed by simulation. This design and simulation have been optimized chip products have been completed.

articleTitle: Fast reliability scheduling algorithm for the static segment of FlexRay for vehicle network
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: The FlexRay is a vehicle network communication protocol, which has been widely used in automotive. X-by wire is the most common application in FlexRay, such as brake by wire and throttle by wire. However, there isn't any mechanism can prevent transient fault. A new Fast Reliability Scheduling Algorithm (FRSA) is proposed to improve communication reliability and safety. The proposed method reduces probability of transient fault in one clock cycle by re-transmission message to ensure system reliability, and improves computational complexity using lookup table method. Experimental results show that the proposed method reduces 86.31% on execution time and 45.02% on slot utilization.

articleTitle: Probabilistic reverse nearest neighbors on uncertain data streams
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In these days, many applications of IoT, Big Data, and Cloud computing have been proposed and discussed. One of the common important issues in these applications is data processing. The data to be considered now have the properties of velocity, veracity, and volume. Uncertain data streams simultaneously have these properties. Reverse nearest neighbors (RNN) query finds the objects that have the query as the nearest object and plays an important in many applications. We thus study probabilistic RNN (PRNN) query over the uncertain data streams in this paper. Due to the uncertainty, the computation overhead for updates gets much higher and how to reduce the computation cost becomes challenging. We provide efficient PRNN query processes over uncertain data streams in terms of time. Our methods can effectively prune the irrelevant data objects and keep only the possible ones for further updates, thus saving time. The proposed methods are also validated through extensive simulation experiments.

articleTitle: A dualband six-phase voltage-control oscillator
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: The voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) by using single-ended delay cell architecture has the advantages of low power consumption, small chip area and large output swing. However, the conventional even-phase outputs ring-type VCO cannot be implemented by single-ended delay cells. This paper presents a dualband six-phase ring type VCO, and it is implemented by the proposed single-ended delay cell. The proposed VCO both with the advantages of single-ended delay cells and the functions of differential delay cells. Moreover, the delay cell has the band switch function, which can improve the VCO performance of jitter. The proposed VCO can be operated at 890-1080 MHz. The peak-to-peak jitter and the root mean square (RMS) jitter are the 35.5 ps and 2.8 ps (at 1 GHz), respectively. Maximal power consumption approximated 6.4 mW at 1.8 V of the supply voltage in a United Microelectronics Corporation 0.18-μm RF CMOS process. The area of the chip is 0.195×0.208 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Radio-frequency magnetron sputtering deposited ZnO-based TFBAR for humidity sensor applications
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This article investigates a thin-film bulk acoustic-wave resonator (TFBAR) based on Li-doped ZnO (LZO) film. The LZO thin-film is deposited by radio frequency (RF) magnetron sputtering system and post-treated with ultraviolet (UV)-ozone illumination. The microstructural and chemical evolutions via various illumination times of the predominantly c-axis orientation LZO films are investigated. The largest piezoelectric coefficient (12.66 pC/N) of the LZO film is obtained after 90 min UV-ozone illumination, which can be ascribed to better crystallization and fewer oxygen-related defects. Furthermore, the fabricated TFBAR exhibits a high quality factor (Q = 1358) at ~500 MHz and a good sensitivity under several relative humidity levels (30~90% at room temperature in a standard atmosphere). The experimental results verify the LZO-based TFBAR is a candidate for humidity sensor applications.

articleTitle: High mobility tungsten-doped thin-film transistor on polyimide substrate with low temperature process
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: A novel high mobility channel material, amorphous tungsten doped indium-oxide, is used as the active layer of flexible TFT, which is fabricated on a transparent polyimide under a low temperature process. The effects of channel thickness are investigated as well in this work. The flexible TFT with a suitable thickness of IWO film shows a high carrier mobility and low sub-threshold swing. The improvement can be attributed to increased donor-like oxygen vacancy with the thickness of channel layer increased.

articleTitle: A novel shot detection approach using 8-neighbors and key-colors
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Shot is often used as basic unit for both analyzing and retrieving video. The approach for automatic shot detection, using the texture character of eight neighbors, is better than traditional one on efficiency. For improving the accurate rate, this method is combined with the color information by adding key colors extraction. At last the result of experiment is given to approve the validity of the method.

articleTitle: A unified quantum scaling length model for nanometer multiple-gate MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Based on the zero-point energy E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> induced by one-dimensional/two-dimensional (1-D/2-D) quantum confinement effects, a unified quantum scaling length model λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">QM</sub> is developed for the nanometer multiple-gate (MG) MOSFETs. It indicates that the quantum scaling length λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">QM</sub> is sensitive to the silicon thickness and the MG MOSFETs abiding by the quantum scaling curves will well control the threshold voltage variation AV<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sub> caused by QMEs. This model not only efficiently evaluates the nanometer MG MOSFETs according to the quantum scaling factor (α<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">QM</sub>), but also provides the basic scaling theory for the device engineer to well design the nanometer MG MOSFETs.

articleTitle: Digital compensator design for high-frequency hybrid resonant buck converter
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In this paper, the digital compensator for the voltage-mode hybrid resonant buck converter operating in CCM is designed. By observing the simulated and experimental bode plots of the loop gain, the digital signal processor (DSP) has delay, which comes from ZOH and ePWM update. Therefore, the digital compensator design is more difficult than using analog compensator. Finally, a prototype with input voltage of 24V, output voltage of 5 V, and switching frequency of 2MHz is used to verify the influence of digital compensator.

articleTitle: Comparative study of sub-Vt SRAM bitcells based on noise-margin-aware design
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Various bitcells were proposed for sub-threshold (sub-Vt) SRAM design with bit interleaving to deal with multi-bit soft errors. Each proposed bitcell uses its own design strategy, where the half-select issue in bit-interleaved cells has been addressed with distinct tradeoffs. However, a design strategy for one cell may not be practical for another, and it is not trivial to compare these cells just by re-designing them with a specific flow. This paper presents a comparative analysis and design of state-of-the-art bit-interleaved SRAM bitcells with a noise-margin-(NM-) aware design approach, which accounts the NM demand in addition to minimizing the cell area. We also disclose complete bitcell design flows, beginning from step-by-step transistor sizing, noise margin evaluation, to the exploration of the minimum operating voltage (Vmin).

articleTitle: A Laypunov base fuzzy expert knowledge model identify elders fall signal
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper presented a Laypunov base fuzzy expert knowledge model identify human fall signal in wearable device. The older human signal analysis have been a research topic health care fields that algorithms build in wearable device real time detect fall situation. The fuzzy expert knowledge model used knowledge base to identify human fall situation, and we also combined Lyapunov convergent theories to adjust knowledge base. In the experimental results, the fuzzy expert knowledge model analysis human fall signal. In addition, we used wearable device combined BLE (Bluetooth low energy) feedback output response real time.

articleTitle: A surveillance framework based on Facebook and Internet of Things techniques
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper presents a surveillance system which is able to provide live video stream and remote control appliances through chat robot (Chatbot) software of Facebook messenger. The appliances will be bundled with a socket controlled by relay and one MediaTek LinkIt 7697, which is marketed Arduino compatible development board. The surveillance system was built on QBoat Sunny, a home Internet of Things (IoT) gateway supplied by Taiwan QNAP Corp. with built-in Linux and numerous functions.

articleTitle: A fast-response buck converter with load-current-extracted and AVDE techniques
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: A fast-response buck converter with load-current-extracted and analog-voltage-dynamic-estimation (AVDE) techniques is proposed in this paper to improve previous works. The transient responses of the proposed buck converter are very fast when load changes between heavy load and light load. The switching frequency of the proposed buck converter is 0.5 MHz for nominal 3.3 V input and 1.0∼2.5 V output range application. The experimental results prove that the proposed scheme improves the transient response within 2.5 us and its maximum power efficiency can be up to 94.76%. The transient-response time of the proposed converter is only within 1.25 switching cycle. The maximum load current is 300 mA. The proposed buck converter has been fabricated with a commercial 0.35 um CMOS 2P4M process, and the total chip area is about 1.245 ×1.02 mm2, including PADs.

articleTitle: Clustering for reduction of power consumption and area on post-silicon delay tuning
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Due to progressing process technology, yield of chips is reduced by timing violation caused by delay variation of gates and wires in fabrication. Recently, post-silicon delay tuning, which inserts programmable delay elements (PDEs) into clock tree before the fabrication and sets the delays of the PDEs to recover the timing violation after the fabrication, is promising to improve the yield. In an existing method, since the PDE is constructed by a buffer chain and a demultiplexer and it is inserted for each register, power consumption and circuit area are increased drastically in comparison with conventional clock synchronous circuits. In this paper, a PDE structure is proposed to reduce the circuit area. Moreover, a clustering method, in which some PDEs are merged into a PDE and a PDE is inserted for multiple registers, is proposed to reduce the power consumption and the circuit area. In computational experiments, the proposed method reduced the power consumption and the circuit area in comparison with the existing method.

articleTitle: Steep switch-off of In0.18Al0.82N/AlN/GaN on Si MIS-HEMT
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: InAlN/Al/GaN HEMT directly on Si for steep subthreshold slope (<;60mV/dec) is demonstrated in this study, and is attributed to displacement charge transition effect. The material analysis with High-Resolution X-ray Diffraction (HR-XRD) and the relaxation by reciprocal space mapping (RSM) are performed to confirm Indium barrier composition and epitaxy quality. The proposed InAlN barrier HEMTs exhibits high ON/OFF ratio with 7 magnitudes and a steep SS is also obtained with subthreshold swing (SS) = 99 mV/dec for forward sweep and SS = 28 mV/dec for reverse sweep.

articleTitle: Effect of different partial pressure on Ga-doped ZnO UV photodetectors by RF sputtering
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Ga-doped zinc oxide metal-semiconductor-metal ultraviolet photodetectors were fabricated by radio frequency magnetron sputtering on quartz substrates. The films' Ga content were relatively high to enlarge the bandgap and obtain low dark current. In addition, it was found that the devices' performance was significantly improved by proper gas flow ratios of O2/Ar during deposition. The responsivity and UV-to-visible rejection ratio of photodetector were 16.08 A/W and 5.44×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> at 10 V applied bias with 280 nm illumination.

articleTitle: Study of the silicon photonic integrated circuits with grating coupler
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This research is focused on the silicon photonic integrated circuits with grating coupler. The system creates a grating structure on a waveguide or substrate. It uses light gratings to guide light into a waveguide or substrate. The coupling efficiency of the grating is lower relative to the prism. Some of the incident light will be directly absorbed by the substrate. Its advantage is reusable.

articleTitle: One-dimensional MAGFET device with a polysilicon cross-shaped hall plate
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper presents a macro model of a one-dimensional (1-D) magnetic MOSFET (MAGFET) with a differential polysilicon cross-shaped Hall plate (CSHP) designed to eliminate the offset voltage and to enlighten measured Hall voltage. Additionally, a readout circuit consists of a pre-amplifier, a low-pass filter, and off-chip instrumental amplifier (IA) with 30 dB, is designed to amplify the output Hall voltage with a gain of 40 dB. Measurements reveal that the maximum output Hall voltage V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H</sub>, the optimum current-related magnetosensitivity S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RI</sub>, the optimum voltage-related magnetosensitivity S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RV</sub>, the averaged nonlinearity error NLE, and the relative bias current I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">bias</sub> are 4.381 mV, 520.5 V/A·T, 40.04 V/V·T, 7.19%, and 200 μA, respectively, for the proposed 1-D MAGFET with a polysilicon CSHP and readout circuit.

articleTitle: Relative indexed compressed sparse filter encoding format for hardware-oriented acceleration of deep convolutional neural networks
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: To address memory and computation resource limitations for hardware-oriented acceleration of deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs), we present a computation flow, stacked filters stationary flow (SFS), and a corresponding data encoding format, relative indexed compressed sparse filter format (CSF), to make the best of data sparsity, and simplify data handling at execution time. And we also propose a three dimensional Single Instruction Multiple Data (3D-SIMD) processor architecture to illustrate how to accelerate deep CNNs by taking advantage of the SFS flow and CSF format. Comparing with the state-of-the-art result [1], our methods achieve 1.11 x improvement in reducing the storage required by AlexNet, and 1.09 x improvement in reducing the storage required by SqueezeNet, without loss of accuracy on the ImageNet dataset. Moreover, using these approaches, chip area for logics handling irregular sparse data access can be saved (about 19.1% chip area in [2]). Comparing with the 2D-SIMD processor structures in DVAS, ENVISION, etc., our methods achieve about 3.65x processing element (PE) array utilization rate improvement (from 26.4% to 96.5%) on the data from Deep Compression on AlexNet <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>.

articleTitle: A fully integrated voltage controlled phase shifter with lossless active inductors
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper presents a method to design a voltage controlled phase shifter in the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) 0.18-μm 1P6M CMOS process. The proposed phase shifter includes series hybrid structure and terminated ports2 and port3 of the hybrid with MOS varactor, however, the active inductors was used instead. The S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> and phase controlled performance get greatly improved. The chip size of the proposed phase shifter could also be reduced. The simulation results showed that a small variation in S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> (0.64±0.19dB) with the control voltage changing from -0.5V to 1V.

articleTitle: Near-field flat focusing mirrors with an transverse invariance
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper shows the different configuration of the near-field flat focusing optics, especially for reflective devices. The physical background to the different focusing mechanisms of near- and far-field focusing is discussed in this paper. These flat focusing mirrors have their transverse invariance, hardly achieved by conventional lenses and engineered planar metalenses.

articleTitle: An open environment wireless sensing framework based on IEEE 802.11ah
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper presents an open environment wireless sensing framework which reports data through wireless wide area network (WAN). It has low power consumption feature by Sigfox, and this new worldwide low power WAN communication technology is based on IEEE 802.11ah.

articleTitle: The design of an automatic safety valve testing system
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: The safety valve is a safety device extensively used in such pressure systems as pressure vessel, boiler and pressure piping for guaranteeing the safe operation of pressure systems. This paper proposes an automatic safety valve testing system, which allows the user to set various test parameters. The system can open the test channel of corresponding pressure range automatically according to the working pressure of safety valve, and implement complete safety valve testing operation automatically. The measured pressure data can be recorded automatically in the testing process, and then the pressure curve can be drawn. Finally, the safety valve test report is exported automatically, so as to display the recorded data and the drawn pressure diagram as criteria for the user to judge whether the safety valve function is abnormal or not. This system can reduce the manual operation cost of safety valve test a lot and increase the accuracy of test greatly.

articleTitle: Linear-cavity mode-locked laser using Thulium-doped nanoengineered yttrium-alumina silica fiber
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In this work, we successfully develop a mode-locked fiber lasers utilizing a nano-engineered Tm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>-doped yttrium-alumina-silica (YAS) glass fiber and a semiconductor saturable absorber mirror (SESAM). The gain fiber, produced by Dr. M. C. Paul's group in CSIR, India, presents several benefits, including high efficiencies and low loss.

articleTitle: Uniform resistive switching properties of sol-gel multilayered BaTiNiOx memory device
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: The modification of multilayered barium titanate nickelate (BTN) thin films on ITO/glass substrate is adopted to enhance the device performance. The XPS analysis reveals the concentration of oxygen vacancies can be reduced by the increasing number of the BTN layer. In addition, the Ni acts as clusters and plays a critical role in the formation/rupture of cone-shaped conductive paths during resistive switching, which promotes the local alignment of oxygen vacancies among metallic-Ni clusters. Thus, the sol-gel BTN memory devices with high ON/OFF ratio and excellent current distribution can be achieved.

articleTitle: Application of electrical impedance on measurement of voidfraction in two-phaseflow
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper presents a method to measure the void fraction in two-phase flow. The method would make a calibration curve and compare to previous equation. In addition, the impedance could be used to measure local void fraction. The present method demonstrates a successful application of practical two-phase flow measurement.

articleTitle: ITO/AgNW/ITO stacked flexible electrodes
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This study demonstrated that the use of a ITO/AgNW/ITO stacked structure could considerably enhance the mechanical flexibility of a transparent conducting oxide while minimizing AgNWs caused rough surface morphology. The bending test showed the electrical resistance variation of the stacked film could reach 1% much lower than that of the initial ITO of 32%. The top ITO also improve the adhesion of AgNWs on ITO. Optimization on the thickness of AgNWs and top ITO layer is necessary for better optical and surface morphological characteristics.

articleTitle: Reliability study of hybrid wide drain poly-Si FinTFT
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In this work, the hot carrier reliability of polycrystalline silicon (poly-Si) fin-like TFT (FinTFT) is investigated. The changes in transconductance (gm), threshold voltage (Vth) and on resistance (Ron) are measured and analyzed. Device with hybrid wide drain design shows minor degradation at the VG = VD stress condition.

articleTitle: Deposition of polymer films by atmospheric pressure plasma
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In this study, we investigate the effects of radio frequency of power and gas flow rates on the chemical compositions of atmospheric He plasma. A customized plasma system was setup and equipped with a radio frequency power supply and an optical emission/absorption spectrometer to help characterizing the plasma. For the deposition of thin polymer films, lactic acid is chosen for its chemical stability, biocompatibility and biodegradability. The properties, compositions and microstructures of deposited films are also investigated to assure the success of deposition.

articleTitle: The fiber grating rain gauge
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In this paper we propose a novel rain gauge by using a fiber Bragg grating with the sensitively of 0.0294nm/mm for the measuring range from 0 to 140mm. The operation mechanism is based on the rain weight to load the thin film of rain gauge and then to stretch the grating to result in the grating wavelength shift.

articleTitle: GIDL effect observed in FinFET shapes and Vt implant energy
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: The leakage of FinFETs with the different features and V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sub> implant energy is observed and strongly related to the previous factors. Due to the process controllability, especially in photo-lithography, the multi-channel shape to promote the drive current seems not easy to be controlled well and deteriorates the desired target. The GIDL effect coming from the lower V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sub> implant energy is more distinct than at the higher with the multi-channel FinFETs. However, this phenomenon was not apparently observed in the single FinFET.

articleTitle: Biometrie identification of persons in a vehicle
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Nowadays in the era of Smart Cities, the issue of driver identification in a vehicle is becoming more and more popular. Firstly, such identification prevents unauthorised use of the vehicle and secondly, if connected to other systems outside of the vehicle, it provides information on driver's identity to the authorities. This paper discusses the issue of biometrie driver identification by means of 2D face recognition with an image obtained from a thermographic camera placed in the front part of the vehicle interior. The recognition itself is processed with neural network. This method is independent from the lighting situation and it is driver-friendly. The identification process is both - safe and reliable.

articleTitle: Analysis of the passband and stopband of symmetrical metal-dielectric films
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: The passband and stopband of symmetrical metal-dielectric films are calculated and considered in this work by analyzing the equivalent phase thickness through calculation of characteristic film matrix. The passband and stopband are reduced with decreasing wavelength. At extreme long wavelength ranges the metal-dielectric multilayer are transparent. Therefore the first stopband from infinite wavelength are derived here. This analysis can be applied to design for the passband and stopband of a layered metamaterial.

articleTitle: Drive current behaviors of multi N-channel FinFETs under different VT implant energies
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: The adjustment of V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sub> implant energy is basically a non-critical parameter to influence the drive current. According to the measurement of electrical performance, the drive current at the ON or OFF state is similar as channel length L= 0.5 or 10μm and channel width W=0.115μm. However, the difference of current behaviors at L=2μm is distinct for both V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sub> implant energy experiments. The ON current at the lower V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sub> implant energy shows the higher than the other. And the V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sub> value for the tested device with the lower V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sub> implant energy is less than zero, which means the uniformity of V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sub> implant control is very important in manufacturing.

articleTitle: Performance enhancement of organic phototransistors with a hybrid gate dielectric
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Organic phototransistors (OPTs) have been fabricated and characterized with a stacked dielectric layer of PMMA/SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> film. Experimental results show that SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> layer provide an excellent light scattering to enhance the photocurrent under the illuminate because of its mesoporous nanoparticles properties. The optoelectronic characteristics of OPTs show that the I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</sub> is -0.07pA and field-effect mobility is 0.01 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/Vs. OPTs irradiated by the visible light source of 11 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> show I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</sub> raising to -0.17 μA, and μ to 0.026 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/Vs.

articleTitle: Green perovskite CsPbBr3 light-emitting diodes with an ultrathin hole-transporting NiOx film
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In this article, we have demonstrated a novel perovskite light-emitting diode (PeLED) with a sol-gel derived NiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> thin film for efficient hole transport. The fabricated NiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> film is highly transparent which facilitates the achievement of high brightness of our PeLEDs. The troublesome problem of roughness of perovskite is overcome by adding the polymers into the perovskite precursor solution. Via optimizing the device structure, low turn-on voltage of 3.1 V and high luminance of ~3200 cd/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> were achieved.

articleTitle: Anneal effect of Er doped zinc oxide by spray pyrolysis
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Zinc oxide thin films with and without erbium doping were prepared by spray pyrolysis with zinc chloride and erbium acetate precursors. Film thickness profile after 700°C annealing process were analyzed. With the anneal time increase, rough and smooth surface were characterized for the ZnO and ZnO:Er samples respectively. The 10K photoluminescence were applied for the film characterization.

articleTitle: Reducing latency for an Android-based VoIP phone
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper describes a method to reduce the end-to-end latency of a VoIP APP to be executed on an Android operating system. The proposed can effectively reduce the latency from around 600 ms to less than 400 ms. Without additional support from the operating system, this latency is comparable to other commercial VoIP programs.

articleTitle: Radio-frequency energy harvesting chip for ISM 915 MHz antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This study presents a radio-frequency (RF) energy harvesting chip, which is fed with the ISM (industrial, scientific and medical) 915 MHz antenna. The proposed chip includes the RF-DC rectifier, over-voltage protection circuit, low dropout regulator (LDO) and charging control circuit, which are all designed and simulated in standard TSMC 0.18 um 1P6M CMOS process. The off-chip matching network is used not only to obtain the maximum power deliver from antenna to rectifier, but also to have the maximum conversion efficiency. A native MOSFET is adopted to design the RF-DC rectifier with low threshold voltage. According to the simulated results, the input return loss and maximum conversion efficiency are -52.546 dB and 43.6 %, respectively, at the input power of -7 dB m and the ISM band of 915 MHz, which varies from 870 MHz to 996 MHz. The output voltage of the RF-DC rectifier is limited from 1.77 to 1.79 volts as the input power varies from -13 dBm to 10 dBm. Passing through the LDO circuit, a stable voltage of 1.5 V is supplied to the charging control circuit.

articleTitle: Hybrid unicast and multicast video streaming using H.264 SVC and FLUTE for set-top box users
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: The digital set-top box (STB) has evolved to provide not only broadcast channel videos to TV watchers but also streaming videos to mobile device users. The users connected to a STB may request the same video content with disparate bitrate requirements. In this case, applying the conventional multicast or unicast technique causes a waste of transmission bandwidth. To resolve this problem, in this study we realized a novel hybrid multicast and unicast video streaming system. The unicast service was based on MPEG-DASH (Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over Hypertext Transfer Protocol). For multirate streamed users, we incorporated the H.264 SVC (Scalable Video Coding) for bitrate adaptation into the multicast groups under the FLUTE (File Delivery over Unidirectional Transport) protocol. Furthermore, we optimized the system performance that intelligently determined the transmitted video segment and quality level according to the bandwidth efficiency and the marginal quality benefit to users. Simulation results showed that the proposed algorithm effectively reduced the waiting time and enhanced the received video quality of mobile device users.

articleTitle: A study of negative resistance effect of CuxO RRAM fabricated by using a sol-gel method
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In this study, we used a sol-gel method to synthesize copper oxide (CuxO) semiconductor and to fabricate CuxO resistive random access memories (RRAMs).
