An abnormal resistive switching behavior was found in the In/Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>O/N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>-Si RRAM. Negative resistance effect was observed in the low electric field region. The RRAM is highly stable and it can operate over 1000 times under DC switching cycles.

articleTitle: Sputtering and annealing graphene oxide hole-transporting layer for perovskite solar cells
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In this study, the graphene thin films were deposited by reactive radio-frequency magnetron sputter. Then, the graphene thin film was annealing with different temperature in the atmosphere to form graphene oxide (GO) thin films. The solar cell structure was inverted for ITO/Graphene oxide/ CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>PbI<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>/PCBM/Ag. Photovolatic conversion efficiency of the cells based on the different graphene oxide morphologies was analyzed by XRD, SEM, PL, TR-PL and UV-Vis absorption spectra. The power conversion efficiency of the best cell was 1.75%.

articleTitle: Analysis of reconfigurable tunnel field effect transistor for improved current characteristics
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper presents different techniques to improve the current performance of reconfigurable tunnel field effect transistor (RTFET). Homojunction RTFETs are considered in this paper. The current performance of RTFETs designed using different semiconductor material and dielectric material is compared in this paper. Proper selection of gate metal work function plays important role in the RTFET design to get symmetric current behavior. The selection of apt gate work function for different homojunction RTFETs is given in this paper. Technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulations are used to analyze the device performance.

articleTitle: 2-Dimension cluster of multiple correlation coefficient with mutual information applied to hyperspectral image band selection
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: High-dimensional datasets suffer from the curse of dimensionality. It influences the accuracy of imaging classification. Thus, the hyperspectral image processing usually selects specific bands to reduce data dimensionality. In our previous work, a particle swarm optimization (PSO) combined with partial correlation coefficient and multiple correlation coefficient is proposed to overcome the traditional method. It proposed two-dimension impurity function band prioritization (2D-IFBP) method to improve the performance of reduction dimension for hyperspectral images. However, due to the limited effects, this method cannot process in the sense of complete two-dimensional orders. To overcome this drawback, a multiple correlation coefficient matrix using PSO to cluster eigenspace and select representative bands is proposed in this paper. The proposed 2D cluster of multiple correlation coefficient with mutual information method is a complete 2D process to obtain the correlation between bands. The effectiveness of the proposed method is evaluated by AVIRIS dataset. The experimental results show that the proposed method can stably select representative bands and obtain the high accuracy.

articleTitle: Low-temperature ZnO films as electron transporting layers for perovskite-based solar cells
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In this study, a low-temperature sol-gel deposited ZnO thin film was used as the electron-transport layer in planar type CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>PM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> perovskite-based solar cells. The CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>PM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> films was prepared via a two-step spin-coating method and the relationship of the concentration of methylammonium iodide (CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>NHI) was discussed. Devices fabricated based on the ZnO coated on glass and with flexible substrates are discussed. The results show that we can achieve a record efficiency of 13.5% (glass) and 10.2% (PET) under AM1.5G irradiation for the low-temperature prepared ZnO based planar type perovskite solar cell.

articleTitle: Wireless charging platform for dual-band magnetic resonance
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This text investigates a dual-band wireless charging platform utilizing magnetic resonance. The platform operates at 6.78 and 13.56 MHz, and is capable of charging two mobile devices simultaneously. Physical measurements of the resonant coils indicate that the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> for 13.56 MHz and the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</inf> for 6.78 MHz are −29.45 and −26.87 dB, respectively. The S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> values of the receiving coil for 6.78 and 13.56 MHz are 24.12 and 19.98 dB, respectively. Furthermore, the effect between the two different frequencies of the transmitter coil is low when they both work simultaneously, implying that the platform can charge batteries for several mobile devices simultaneously. The S parameters can be used to calculate the efficiency of the wireless charging platform, which is approximately 33.11% at 6.78 MHz and 25.12% at 13.56 MHz. Furthermore, the results indicate that the efficiency of the rectifier circuits is greater than 50% at 6.78 MHz and greater than 80% at 13.56 MHz.

articleTitle: Impact of post deposition annealing on resistive switching in Ga2O3-based conductive-bridge RAM devices
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: We study the influence of post-deposition annealing on the electrical properties of performance of Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-based Cu-ion-based conductive-bridge RAM (CBRAM) devices. Amorphous gallium oxide (Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>) thin films were fabricated by RF sputtering at room temperature. The deposited films were annealed from the different temperatures and gas ambient. Their resistive switching characteristics are compared to determine the role of temperature and atmosphere in the annealing process on performance of these memory devices. The substantial improvement in device performance, such as stable switching, high switching cycles, and increased memory window, were obtained in the CBRAM devices during the post-Ga203 deposition annealing in pure nitrogen (N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) ambient.

articleTitle: Fast transient buck converter with adaptive threshold voltage control
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive threshold voltage (ATV) control to realize a fast transient buck converter. The ATV control can reduce feedback delay, saturate duty cycle, mitigate output transient ripple and suppress output voltage ringing. Thus, the transient response of the buck converter can be enhanced during load current changes while switching frequency of the buck converter can be kept constant at steady state. A prototype converter with the ATV control was designed with 0.35-μm 2P4M CMOS technology. The simulation results demonstrate that the recovery time of the buck converter with the ATV control is less than 3 μs when load current changes between 500 mA and 0 mA.

articleTitle: One-comparator sampling design for digital power converters
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: One-comparator sampling design for the digital power converter is presented herein. The one-comparator sampling method is quite simple without any actual analog-to-digital converter. However, how to design it has not been studied. Consequently, in this paper, in order to design the digital power converter based on one-comparator sampling, the associated mathematical deductions are provided firstly, and a design example is given secondly.

articleTitle: Low current harmonies PWM for tow-level three-phase grid-connected PV inverter
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: The advantages of photovoltaic (PV) power generation include no fuel cost and abundance of sunlight. For the grid-connected PV inverter systems, the efficiency is always an important issue. At the PV panel side, a DC/DC converter with maximum power point tracking operation is always used to improve power generation of the system. Further, at the grid-connected inverter side, the generated active power is proportional to the power generation efficiency. Therefore, the grid current is expected to be in phase with the grid voltage and the current harmonics must be low to avoid excessive losses. In this paper, a switching strategy is proposed to generate the grid current with low harmonics. Both baseband harmonics and the side-band harmonics are considered. In the simulation, it is shown that a 79.5% reduction of baseband harmonics and a 34% reduction of the total harmonics distortion are achieved comparing with the conventional switching strategy. The direct advantage is the improvement of the system efficiency.

articleTitle: Fabrication and characterization of a sensitivity multi-annular backscattered electron detector for desktop SEM
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: A sensitivity silicon p-n diodes for detecting backscattering electrons in SEM was proposed and fabricated. The multi-annular configuration enables to provide higher sensitivity of Z-contrast and better surface topography contrast of BSE image. In this study, the multi-annular backscattered electron detector (BSED) can provide enhancement of surface topography contrast and image contrast with 105% and 42% as compared with commercial BSED which with the multi-fan configuration. We also designed a high sensitivity to low energy electrons detector which with lateral p-n junctions and Al metal grids.

articleTitle: On the RF energy harvesting based on CMOS technology
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: RF energy harvesting has been recognized as one of the possible options for powering embedded and remote electronic devices. There are technologies and products, such as wireless charging, RFID systems, remote charging, available which have demonstrated the technical feasibilities provides that the power level of the RF sources are sufficient. However for ambient low-power RF energy harvesting, it is still a quite challenging technical issue. Due to the regulation on RF power level emission in the available systems and the use the mainstream digital CMOS technology for implementation, the achievable power level and power efficiency are still far below the requirements of most applications. To maximize the conversion efficiency and to acquire sufficient energy, optimal designs for every building blocks of the harvesting system are required. This review highlights some methods to enhance the RF/DC conversion such as using low-threshold PMOS devices, body biasing, gate compensation, for full-wave rectifying, low-loss CMOS switches for charge pump design, and adaptive voltage regulation using pulse-skipping modulation technique.

articleTitle: Design of a 5GS/s 200 MHz BW 74.8 dB SNDR continuous-time sigma delta modulator in 28nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: A wide-band continuous-time sigma delta modulator (CTSDM) targeting intermediate-frequency (IF) digitizing is presented. This modulator uses a feedforward/feedback hybrid structure to lower the peaking of out-of-band in signal transfer function (STF). The continuous time self-coupling (CTSC) integrator is introduced to enhance noise shaping. The modulator in 28nm CMOS process is clocked at 5GHz with oversampling ratio (OSR) of 12.5. With 200 MHz signal bandwidth, simulation results show that it achieves a peak signal-to-noise-plus-distortion ratio (SNDR) of 74.8 dB and spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) of 90.8dB with high power efficiency.

articleTitle: Fabrication and characterization of planar-type top-illuminated high-responsivity InP-based avalanche photodetector for 10 Gbps optical receiver applications
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In this work, a planar-type top-illuminated high-responsivity InP-based avalanche photodetector (APD) was fabricated and characterized. The dark current of 0.55 nA, capacitance of 0.237 pF, responsivity of 12.2 A/W were obtained when APD operated at 0.95 breakdown voltage (Vbr). The eye diagrams of the fabricated APD under 0.95 VBR to the pseudorandom NRZ code of length 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">31</sup>-1 at 2.5–10 Gb/s were measured. The absence of significant intersymbol interference and the error free for the signals up to 10 Gb/s can be achieved.

articleTitle: The μeq fitting for mixed current model of MOSFETs considering horizontal electric field
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: The modulation of equivalent channel mobility μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eq</sub> can fit the accurate drain current in high accuracy as the change of horizontal electrical field, related to the drain bias and the channel length with fixed gate bias. The fitting I-V curves contain long, middle and short-channel devices. In this model, the short channel effect, reverse short channel effect, DIBL are taken into consideration to satisfying the whole reliable drive current model.

articleTitle: A 10b 160-MS/s domino-SAR ADC in 90nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper presents a 10b 160-MS/s SAR ADC with the domino-SAR operation. The capacitor swapping technique is used to effectively remove the major capacitor-DAC transition error, resulting in improved linearity, without needing a large total capacitance. The ADC was implemented in 90nm CMOS. It consumes a total power of 2mW from a 1.2V supply. The simulated peak SNDR and SFDR are 59.8dB and 76dB respectively. The Nyquist ENOB is 9.5 bits, equivalent to a FOM of 17.3fJ/conversion-step.

articleTitle: An upgrade of ESD-reliability in HV 60-V nLDMOS-SCR devices by the discrete anode
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Discrete modulation was applied to a 60 V nLDMOS drain-side inserted SCR npn-arranged type and pnp-arranged type to investigate the devices' electrostatic discharge (ESD) protection ability. When applying SCR npn-arranged type discrete-anode modulation to the drain side, a transmission-line-pulse test revealed that the I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t2</sub> slightly increased. When the discrete parameter was 91 sets, the most favorable I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t2</sub> was 2.157 A. Compared with the npn-arranged type, the SCR pnp-arranged type with discrete modulation applied to the anode had strong SCR characteristics. I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t2</sub> increased to more than 7 A. In addition, under discrete modulation, the SCR npn-arranged and pnp-arranged types had clearly higher current density. Using the discrete method, each P+ OD's ability to discharge ESD current thus increased.

articleTitle: Improving operation electric field of Cu-based resistive switching memory by Cu chemical displacement technique
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Among the novel non-volatile memories, the electrochemical metallization (ECM)-type Resistive Random Access Memory (ReRAM) stands out from all the competitors. ECM-type memories use active metals as the electrode, such as copper. However, copper is hard to pattern by using dry etch. Therefore in this study, the copper chemical displacement technique (CDT) was applied to form the electrode of ReRAM device. We used CDT-Cu to solve the etch problem and improve the electric characteristics of device. The obtained results showed that samples using CDT-Cu exhibited lower set electric field than that of sample without CDT-Cu. The current density in the LRS, as well as operation electrical field, was also improved by CDT-Cu method. The retention of CDT-Cu sample can retain over 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> seconds.

articleTitle: Enhancement of optoelectronic properties on Al-doped ZnO ultra-thin film by using a multiple buffer layers process in nitrogen atmosphere
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In this study, the multiple buffer layers process with various N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> atmosphere is designed to enhance the optoelectronic properties of 80nm Aluminum-doped ZnO (AZO) ultra-thin film. At first, the different multiple buffer layers of 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 had been deposited, the lowest resistance is 9.1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> after three multiple layers process. Then, the different quantity of nitrogen (0, 0.4, 0.8, 1.2, 1.6 sccm) had been done and the lowest resistivity is 4.3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> Ω-cm by using 0.4 sccm N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> atmosphere and the average transmittance from 400 to 800 nm is about 93.7%, the optimum figure of merit (FOM) is 9.7 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> Ω<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. The results promote the application of AZO on transparent conductive thin film could be deposited in simple process.

articleTitle: Explore connection fault handling strategies of third-party libraries by AOP
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In a distributed system, programs interact with each other to achieve its functionality. To build a robust system, developers should care about exception handling. This paper propose a dynamic analysis method to explore exception handling strategies of a third-party library without looking code. In result section, we explore an operation which connects to a MySQL server.

articleTitle: Quasi-Yagi antenna with PBG structure for dual band RFID applications
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: A dual-band quasi-Yagi antenna with a photonic bandgap structure for radio frequency identification (RFID) applications is presented in this paper. The meander line of the quasi-Yagi antenna was designed to operate at 900 MHz, exciting the upper resonant mode for operation at the 2.45-GHz band. The obtained impedance bandwidths were 160 MHz (approximately 18.18%) and 97 MHz (approximately 4%) for covering the required bandwidths of the RFID ultra-high-frequency band (860-960 MHz) and microwave band (2.4-2.48 GHz), respectively. The proposed antenna also provides omni-radiation patterns at 900 MHz and end-fire direction radiation patterns at 2.45 GHz with maximum peak antenna gains of 0.1 and 3.4 dBi, respectively.

articleTitle: A fast graph based method for object segmentation in sidescan sonar image
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Sidescan sonar image is a key step for marine object recognition and classification, and still remains a challenging task as the images formed from acoustic signal are severely interfered with noise. Moreover, its real time processing is indispensable for subsea robots. In this paper, we proposed a fast and precise method to implement real-time object segmentation. The method integrates preprocessing using a graph-based bothway spanning forest(BSF) algorithm and fine segmentation using level sets method with region-scalable fitting (RSF) model. The formal part is developed from the minimum/maximum spanning tree algorithm, which deals with sonar images efficiently and provides a coarse segmentation result as the initial input of the latter part, and then RSF model refines that result and obtains a final object segmentation. Our method achieves a faster speed by 2 s per image (14000*80) compared to the related work and a perfect segmentation accuracy, which outperforms the state-of-art method.

articleTitle: Electrical characteristics of WO3/Ag/WO3 sandwich structure fabricated with magnetic-control sputtering metrology
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Using the magnetic-control sputtering fabrication, WO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>/Ag/WO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> thin film was successfully formed as a sandwich structure treated as a transparent conductive thin film. The thicknesses of silver and tungsten oxide were 10 to 20nm and 50 to 60nm, respectively. For the increase of silver thickness from 10 to 20nm, the sheet resistance is reduced. However, this effect in tungsten oxide is entirely reversed. As the electrical measurement was applied to this tested sandwich structure, the conductivity is better than that for the single layer of tungsten oxide due to the conduction contribution from the silver layer.

articleTitle: Study of the process in Gallium doped ZnO thin film to apply on plus sensor
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In this study, the "Intermittence Process" and "Inserted nano Ag particles process" are designed to deposit Gallium-doped ZnO (GZO) thin film and apply on pulse sensor. 300nm GZO thin films had been deposited on a flexible (PC) substrate by radio frequency (RF) sputtering. Intermittence process is designed to improve the quality of the GZO thin film. In order to increase the mobility of carriers, the Cu electrode is used in this process. Another process is to insert the nano Ag particles in GZO thin film without Cu electrode, due to the Ag material has excellent conductive. Two processes of thin film are compared with the change rate of resistivity and mobility after different loading test treatment. As the result, the higher and more stable sensitive of resistance change rate is the process of GZO layer after intermittence process, which has the lowest resistance is 9.98×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>Ω-cm at IN1 treatment, after the Cu electrode is treated to assistance as device, which is proven to have better use on plus sensor now.

articleTitle: Optical coherence tomography — From micron to nanometer resolution
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In vivo and high-speed optical coherence tomography (OCT) on cells and tissues with sub-micron resolution could help unveil functions of living organisms and facilitate clinical disease/cancer diagnosis in the early stage. With extreme ultraviolet as the light source, nanometer-resolution OCT could be realized to extend its applications in 3D nanostructure inspection.

articleTitle: The characteristics of the gallium-doped zinc oxide films using radio frequency magnetron sputtering
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Transparent conductive gallium-doped zinc oxide (GZO) thin films with different deposition power (from 75 to 150 W) were prepared on the Coring glass substrate by using R.F. magnetron sputtering method. The resulting GZO thin films were crystalline, displaying a hexagonal wurtzite-type crystal structure with a preferred grain orientation in the (002) direction. The best FOM was obtained at 125 W.

articleTitle: Car 2 infrastructure use case development progress
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This document deals with integration of a recent semiconductor components within rapidly growing automotive sector. Researchers combined advanced technologies and proven car communication concepts aiming to development of demanded functionalities and demonstrating them on two use cases. Researchers started with technology analysis, have done defined experiments on the new components and specified representative use cases. Outcomes of the research will address two main stakeholder groups — car users and vehicle infrastructure operators enabling them entirely new comfort of taking care of vehicles both on professional and user basis.

articleTitle: Theoretical investigation of the signal gain in heavily Ho3+-doped silicate fiber
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: We have theoretically investigated the small gain per unit length of a Ho<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>-doped fiber with high ion concentrations. The gain fiber, produced by Dr. S. Jiang's group in Advalue photonics, USA, presents several benefits, including high optical efficiencies and low propagation loss.

articleTitle: The improved performance on organic light emitting diodes using different hole transporting layers
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: The research reports the fabrication of organic light-emitting devices (OLEDs) with (N'-bis(1-naphthyl)-N, N'-dipheny l-1, 1' biphenyl 4, 4'-dimaine) (NPB) and 4, 4'-Cyclohexylidenebis[N, N-bis(4-methyl-phenyl)benzenamine] (TAPC) hole transporting layer (HTL) materials. With a kept 1000 cd/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of luminance density, the driving voltage of OLEDs with NPB and TAPC were 5.5 V and 6.5 V, respectively. It was also found that we can achieve the large luminance and transport efficiency from the proposed OLEDs with the use of NPB layer.

articleTitle: Luminance compensation design using modified histogram equalization for driving assistance system under night vision
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Night Vision Assistant can offer safety for the pedestrians at night, but the clarity of the capturing video has historically been an issue and needed to be improved. This paper focuses on applying MATLAB (Matrix Laboratory) for determining how the image should be modified through back-propagation neural network, and the image will be adjusted for better luminosity automatically through the modified algorithm of histogram equalization. The result shows that the modified image can be more easily discernable, as well as the distortion problems caused by overexposure and underexposure can be improved.

articleTitle: Feasibility study for dispersed bubbly flow and other flow patterns spectrum boundary by probability density function
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In this study, a two-phase flow experiment has been carried out to investigate the feasibility of using probability density function for distinguishing dispersed bubbly flow from the flow regime map. The conductivity sensors were installed and used to acquire the transient conductivity signals, which have been converted to void fraction values during the tests. The Matlab software was used to draw the probability density function of void fraction, and it appears clear differences among the probability density function of void fraction in different flow patterns. Based on this, the probability density function is used to identify the boundary of dispersed bubble flow. By obtaining the important features of the probability density function profiles such as peak location, maximum/minimum values and area ratios of covered regions, the boundary of dispersed bubble flow can be identified.

articleTitle: Tunneling-assisted carrier transfer in pentacene-based thin-film transistors with a MoO3 buffer layer
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Excellent electrical characteristics of pentacene-based OTFTs with a PMMA dielectric layer were obtained by inserting a MoO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> buffer layer, including high mobility of 0.48 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/Vs, the threshold voltage of -11.5 V, and a on/off current ratio of 7.7 ×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>. In the electrical characteristics, we found the tunneling-effect existed in the devices with the MoO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> buffer layer. From the x-ray photoelectron spectroscopic results on MoO3/pentacene interface, the occurrence of certain chemical reaction and thus formation of a self-assembled layer as the carrier tunneling path were confirmed for the 1.3 eV shift of the binding energy of C1s core level peak in the interface. The self-assembled layer did not hinder the carriers from injecting, instead, it enhanced the carrier tunneling. This phenomenon was systematically studied in this letter.

articleTitle: Optimization of stacking graphene layers as a saturable absorber for mode-locked lasers
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: The optimization of stacking graphene layers as a saturable absorber (SA) for achieving both wider dynamic range and shorter pulsewidth in mode-locked lasers (MLLs) is demonstrated. This study clearly shows an important conclusion that the lower stacking graphene layers, such as the 5-layer is preferable to use as SA for wider dynamic range and hence better pulse tunability range of 5.1-μW, whereas the higher stacking graphene layers, such as the 17-layer is preferable to use as a SA for providing stable and shorter pulsewidth of 523-fs.

articleTitle: Multi-stacking hybrid P/N/P nanosheet layers junctionless field-effect transistors
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This work demonstrates the hybrid poly-Si nanosheet channels junctionless (JL) field-effect transistors (FET). The hybrid P/N/P double nanosheet channels JL-FFT exhibits the excellent electrical performances in terms of a high I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</inf> current ratio (>10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>), subthreshold swing (176mV/dec), and a small DIBL (13mV/V). These properties are achieved by reducing the effective channel thickness determined by the channel/substrate/channel junction. Furthermore, this stacked hybrid P/N/P double nanosheet channels JL-FET is a promising candidate for high-density 3D stacked IC applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of transient pressure and temperature variations in a subcooled boiling channel under forced vertical excitations
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In this paper, an experimental facility of a subcooled boiling flow loop with a vertical exciter has been constructed and tested to investigate the transient variations of subcooled boiling flow parameters under forced excitations. Various heat fluxes (q"= 6204 and 11029 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) were loaded to the test section under stationary and different forced excitation conditions f= 0, 0.51, 1.06 and 1.62 Hz). The transient signals of differential pressure (DP) and fluid temperature were recorded during the tests, and the fast Fourier transform (FFT) was utilized to analyze the transient data. It was observed that under low frequency excitations (f= 0.51 Hz), the variations of pressure and temperature due to forced excitations were relatively minor and may not be clearly identified by the FFT. Whereas in higher frequency excitations f= 1.06 and 1.62 Hz), the excitation frequencies can be clearly shown in FFT results, which suggests that the flow can be oscillated and the transient variations were observable under the higher frequency forced excitations.

articleTitle: Color stability enhancement of white organic light-emitting diodes
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Hybrid white organic light-emitting diodes (WOLEDs) were prepared and their characteristics were discussed. The blue fluorescent emitter and yellow phosphorescent emitter are fabricated at the seperate layer. Color stability of the WOLEDs were modulated by a charge control layer (CCL) between the two emitting layers. The WOLEDs were optimized and driven at various current densities, its CIE coordinates located at (0.33, 0.51) and varied within (±0.01, ±0.01). Experimental results show that WOLEDs with high color stability have been obtained and are feasible for lighting applications.

articleTitle: Observation of degradation and recovery of stacked HfOx/ZrOy/HfOx MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: The 28nm hafnium-based gate dielectric with a profile of HfO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>/ZrO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sub>/HfO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub> (HZH) was deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD) technology. Different nitridation and annealing process conditions on stacked high-k layers were applied to probe the promotion of device performance. One of the effective stress methods to expose the dielectric integrity is the voltage-ramping dielectric breakdown (VRDB). Using this stress method with forward or backward bias, the degradation or recovery efficiency for the tested devices can be exhibited with the performance of stress induced leakage current (SILC), soft breakdown (SBD), progressive breakdown (PBD), and hard breakdown (HBD). The possible degradation and recovery mechanisms are also studied to figure out the relationship of nitridation and annealing impacting the quality of high-k layers.

articleTitle: Source-assisting full-diversity DQOSTBC in wireless relay networks
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Previously, a source-assisting (SA) traditional distributed quasi-orthogonal space time block code (DQOSTBC) is proposed for a DAF relay network with one source node, one destination node and multiple relay nodes. The SA scheme reduces the number of relay node by one. However, the decoding at the relays may occur and SA traditional DQOSTBC may lose full-diversity. In this paper, we propose full-diversity source-assisting DQOSTBC scheme for three relays. The main contribution is that we design the source-assisting distributed QOSTBC code matrices for 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">^</sup>3=8 cases. Each relay is in AAF or DAF mode when its source-relay channel coefficient is below or above the threshold. The simulation results show that the proposed SA-DQOSTBC outperforms the previous SA-DQOSTBC by 4 dB at 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> bit error rate (BER).

articleTitle: Monolayer-like MAPbI3 film with high charge mobility for solar cells
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: The monolayer-like perovskite films with single crystal cross profile are considered to be the ideal active layer for high efficiency perovskite solar cells (PSCs) owing to the minimization of defects and maximization of charge carrier mobility. To date, how to prepare a high-quality monolithic perovskite film is still a challenge for PSCs. We have been seeking the combined methods for the monolayer-like MAPbI3 film towards high efficiency solar cells. Recently, we have revealed a colloidal strategy to prepare the compact monolayer-like perovskite films by controlling the size of colloidal clusters in the perovskite precursor. According to the space charge limited current, the trap density in the monolithic film was nearly an order of magnitude lower than that of the control samples, while the charge carrier mobility is approaching to that of MAPbI3 single crystal. As a result, the power conversion efficiency of the PSCs is increased to over 20%. These results shed light on the preparation of high quality monolayer-like MAPbI3 films via retarding crystallization and increasing nucleation rate.

articleTitle: The stand-by current performance improvement by reducing post-etch Cu-F residue to prevent Cu extrusion for 28nm-node Cu interconnect and beyond
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Copper (Cu) interconnect at back-end of the line is one of key factors to impact the stand-by current (Isb) performance. However, issue of Cu-loss deteriorates Cu interconnect integration. The formation of Cu-loss is attributed to that fluorine produced by via etching process catalyzes Cu oxidation reaction to form Cu-F. Following up, Cu extrusion of metal lines through by contact vias is carried out. This paper provides the solution to overcome the formation of Cu-loss. The post-etch Cu-F residue plays a key role in forming Cu-loss. By analysis of Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>p<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, using the N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> plasma treatment after via etching reduces 48% of Cu-F. Following up, the additional NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> flush step successfully removes the remaining Cu-F. With the above two steps, Cu extrusion free on the top of contact vias is found. Moreover, 5 times the queue time extension between via etching to tungsten barrier deposition is achieved. Finally, the Isb yield impact by Cu-loss is successfully eliminated, and EM is improved.

articleTitle: Twofold concatenation of space-time coded spatial modulation
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: A new space-time coding scheme is drawn upon the concepts of concatenation, multilevel coding, and spatial modulation. In light of a space-time block coded spatial modulation scheme, several component codes are combined in conjunction with set partitioning of the transmission matrix set according to the coding gain distance criterion. Then, the associated scheme is further concatenated with an outer Reed-Solomon code. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme is superior as regards its bit error performance.

articleTitle: Experimental studies of PbS quantum dot fiber amplifier
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: The PbS quantum dots doped into fiber core as the gain medium has not been proposed. In this study, we change PbS quantum dots concentration and fiber length to identify the strongest fluorescence. Using 793nm semiconductor laser as pump light and 976nm semiconductor laser as signal light, the gains and saturation powers are measured. Experimental results show that this PbS quantum dot optical fiber at pump power of 1.9W, concentration of 1.57 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">23</sup>QDs/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, length of 1.5cm case can reach the fiber amplifier gain 1.72 dB/cm.

articleTitle: Deposition study of stacked zinc oxide — Molybdenum oxide film by spray pyrolysis
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: Stacked zinc oxide-molybdenum oxide thin films with different molybdenum oxide thickness were prepared on silicon substrate by spray pyrolysis with zinc acetate and molybdenum chloride precursors. In the photoluminescence analysis, the zinc oxide related peaks were characterized for all films. With the increase of molybdenum oxide thickness, the near band edge emission corresponded to zinc oxide remains and the donor-exciton and defect-related peaks were inhibited. The band bending between zinc oxide and molybdenum oxide in interface were discussed.

articleTitle: High transparent MAPbBr3 perovskite quantum dots solar cells
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In this study, the MAPbBr3 quantum dots (QD-MAPbBr3) were prepared by the simple and rapid method. Octylammonium bromide (OABr) makes the MAPbBr3 with better exciton binding energy, good surface morphology and stability. To form nanocrystalline thin film, the QD-MAPbBr3 was coated by spin-coating method in a nitrogen-filled glove box. The solar cells structure was ITO/NiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>/QD-MAPbBr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>/C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sub>/Ag, where NiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>, QD-MAPbBr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sub> were used as a hole transport layer, active layer and electron transport layer, respectively. To realize material characteristics, X-ray diffraction (XRD), field-emission scanning electron microscope (FESEM), UV/VIS/NIR spectrometer, and photoluminescence spectrometers (PL) were used to analysis crystallinity, surface morphology, transmittance, and optical behavior of the QD-MAPbBr3 films. The J-V characteristics of devices were evaluated by the solar simulator system.

articleTitle: 2×VDD-tolerant ESD detection circuit in a 90-nm low-voltage CMOS process
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: A new 2×VDD-tolerant electrostatic discharge (ESD) detection circuit using only low-voltage device is proposed in a 90-nm 1-V CMOS process. Unlike the RC based detection circuit, the proposed circuit is a voltage triggered detection circuit, so the clamp device cannot be triggered even under very fast power up events. Also, without RC network the detection circuit generates a very small leakage current. The proposed circuit can generate 50.1 mA current to turn on the substrate triggered silicon-controlled rectifier (STSCR) under the ESD stress. Under normal operating conditions, all the devices are free from over-stress voltage threat, the leakage current is only 50 nA. The simulation result shows the circuit can be used for 2×VDD-tolerant application.

articleTitle: Neuromorphic behavior in nanofloating-gate organic field-effect transistors
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In this paper, we report on novel organic field-effect transistors (OFETs) for neuromorphic applications. The device structure is inspired by conventional floating-gate memories, and it incorporates a few nanometer-thick, surface-oxidized Al film as a semi-transparent charge-trap component. Fabricated on Si and plastic, the OFETs with a pentacene and dinaphto[2,3-b:2',3'-f|thieno[3,2-b]thiophene channel exhibit characteristic long- and short-term activation responses of biological synapses.

articleTitle: The improved performance on organic light emitting diodes using different hole transporting layers
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: The research reports the fabrication of organic light-emitting devices (OLEDs) with (N'-bis(1-naphthyl)-N, N'-diphenyl-1, 1' biphenyl4,4'-dimaine (NPB) and 4,4'-Cyclohexylidenebis[N, N-bis(4-methyl-phenyl)benzenamine] (TAPC) hole transporting layer (HTL) materials. With a kept 1000 cd/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of luminance density, the driving voltage of OLEDs with NPB and TAPC were 5.5 V and 6.5 V, respectively. It was also found that we can achieve the large luminance and transport efficiency from the proposed OLEDs with the use of NPB layer.

articleTitle: CMOS current-reversing circuit
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In this paper, a CMOS current-reversing circuit has been proposed. The layout of the proposed circuit has been made by using the N-well 0.35μm 2p4m process parameters. According to the post-layout simulation results, as the supply voltage is set to 2V, the input current range of the proposed current-reversing circuit can be ±150 μA, the corresponding output linear error is less than 2%, and the output offset current is only -0.321μA. Moreover, the maximum power consumption is 0.42mW and when the input current is 120 μA, the 3-dB bandwidth can be 120 MHz. Simulation results are consistent with the theoretic analysis. The proposed circuit is expected to be useful in current-mode circuits design and other related applications.

articleTitle: Spurs and linearity consideration for aliasing-free pulse-modulated polar transmitters under fewer harmonics in dual-phase operation
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: This paper presents an aliasing-free pulse modulated polar transmitter under fewer harmonics condition for the 4G long term evolution (LTE) femtocell base stations. Compared between two kinds of harmonic conditions K = 1 and 3, the fewer K implementation is capable of reducing the complexity and the number of modulation spurs resulted from the pulse modulator. However, the other outside modulation spurs will still be revealed after non-linear amplification. Based on this reason, the dual-phase digital pulse-width modulation and balanced configuration were adopted to suppress the undesired modulation spurs at the combination output port. A prototype transmitter system was constructed with commercially available components. Measuring using a 10-MHz bandwidth LTE 16-QAM signal at 836.5 MHz for application, it achieves 28% efficiency at 21.2-dBm power level. The condition of K = 3 also has more than 4.3 dB better adjacent channel leakage power ratio than the one of K = 1 under the same memoryless digital pre-distortion based on lookup tables.

articleTitle: A dual-mode fast-transient average-current-mode buck converter without slope-compensation
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: A dual-mode fast-transient average-current-mode buck converter without slope-compensation is proposed in this paper. The benefits of the average-current-mode are fast-transient response, simple-compensation design, and no requirement for slope-compensation, furthermore, that minimizes some power management problems, such as EMI, size, design complexity, and cost. Average-current-mode control employs two loop control methods, an inner loop for current and an outer one for voltage. The proposed buck converter using the current sensing and average-current-mode control techniques can be stable even if the duty cycle is greater than 50%. It which can adaptively switch between pulse-width modulation (PWM) and pulse-frequency modulation (PFM) is operated with very high conversion efficiency. Under light load condition, the proposed buck converter enters PFM mode to decrease the output ripple. That can be switch to PWM mode to realize a smooth transition under heavy load condition. Therefore, PFM is used to improve the efficiency at light load. Dual-mode buck converter has very high conversion efficiency over a wide load conditions. The proposed buck converter has been fabricated with TSMC 0.35μm CMOS 2P4M processes, the total chip area is 1.45 × 1.11mm2. Maximum output current is 450mA at the output voltage 1.8V. When the supply voltage is 3.6V, the output voltage can be 0.8V∼2.8V. Maximum transient response is less than 10μs. Finally, the theoretical analysis is verified to be correct by simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: A dimmable LED driver based on H-bridge and differential-mode transformer
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: A dimmable LED driver based on the H-bridge and current-sharing transformer is presented in this paper. The LED currents are as equal as possible based on the current-sharing transformers. Moreover, the magnitudes of the LED currents can be changed by controlling the duty cycle of one switch, and the conduction time of the LED currents can be adjusted by controlling the duty cycle of the other switch. Accordingly, not only the current-sharing transformers can be demagnetized via the H-bridge without additional components, but also the LED dimming can be achieved without complicated control.

articleTitle: Enhancement of random laser by using silver nanostructre materials
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: The plasmonic random laser have been demonstrated by the dye coated PVA film with embedding of silver nanoparticle that played the role not only the scatter but also the surface plasmon resonance.

articleTitle: Off-state current behaviors of 28nm-node nMOSFETs under negative gate bias
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: The off-state current of MOSFETs under 28nm-node or beyond seems more important than before to keep the long-time operation for mobile electronic products. In this study, we focus on two parts to expose the off-state current behaviors for 28nm nMOSFETs: the drain current under the negative gate bias and the leakage mechanisms of whole devices in off-state, coming from DIBL, GIDL and punch-through effects. Rating the contribution of these three factors and in different channel lengths, DPN nitrogen concentrations and annealing temperatures is chiefly focused.

articleTitle: The study on cold cathode fluorescent lamp as optical microscope light source
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: In the study, using a cold cathode fluorescent lamp with low heat, long lifetime, low light failure and good color rendering index as the microscope light source, and using contrast of color peak signal-to-noise ratio (CPSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM) to compare the microscope images of a rat kidney slice with halogen lamp. The CRI values of a halogen lamp and the CCFL measured by an integrating sphere were 98.6, 85.2, respectively. The images yielded from both the halogen lamp and the CCFL as the light sources had a CPSNR of 26.83 dB and a SSIM of 0.9148. Even if the image from CCFL light source have a little distortion, but the similarity of two images between the halogen and CCFL light source as high as 90%. CCFL has been confirmed to provide microscopic lighting successfully.

articleTitle: Strain relaxation properties of InAsyP1−y metamorphic buffer layers for SWIR InGaAs photodetector
publicationTitle: 2018 7th International Symposium on Next Generation Electronics (ISNE)
abstract: We report on the strain relaxation properties of an InAs<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.43</sub>P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.57</sub>/ In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.73</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.27</sub>As/InAs<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.43</sub>P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.57</sub> triple layer photodetector structure with InAs<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sub>P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-y</sub> metamorphic step-graded buffer layers grown on InP substrate. Reciprocal space mapping (RSM) of (004) reflection along [110] direction show that the InAs<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.3</sub>P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.57</sub> and In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.73</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.27</sub>As slightly tilt toward opposite direction and separates to two lattice points. However, in the RSM of (115) reflection, only one lattice point is observed. Our results indicate the layers fully relaxed in the coordinate system of the substrate, not in that of the tilted layers. TEM analysis indicates that there is no threading dislocation within the InGaAs absorption layer. I-V measurement on the diffusion junction of the detector shows a dark current value of 2.10 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup> A at a bias voltage of -0.5 V, which is among the best of the current state of art. The energy gap obtained from room temperature PL is 0.573 eV, corresponding to a cut-off wavelength of ~2.16 μm.
